header:
import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
noncomputable section
namespace LR
abbrev Idx (l : ℕ) := Fin (l + 1)
def R (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ := Subring.closure {q | ∃ a b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)}
instance rModule (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] : Module (R p) V := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
def MR (p : ℕ) {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V := Submodule.span (R p) (M : Set V)
def DP {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V := (r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹ • f^r
def e {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := DP y i v
def Inv {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U] (W : Submodule F U) (f : Module.End F U) : Prop := ∀ u ∈ W, f u ∈ W
def Brackets {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U] (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop := h*x-x*h = (2:F) • x ∧ h*y-y*h = (-2:F) • y ∧ x*y-y*x = h
def ext {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U] {l : ℕ} (B : Module.Basis (Idx l) F U) (i : ℕ) : U := if hi : i < l+1 then B ⟨i,hi⟩ else 0
def MU {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U] {l : ℕ} (B : Module.Basis (Idx l) F U) (i j : Idx l) : Module.End F U := (B.coord j).smulRight (B i)
def Actions {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U] (l : ℕ) (a : ℕ → U) (x y h : Module.End F U) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) : Prop :=
 x (a 0) = 0 ∧ (∀ i, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ l → x (a i) = ((l-i+1 : ℕ):F) • a (i-1)) ∧ (∀ i, i ≤ l → y (a i) = ((i+1:ℕ):F) • a (i+1)) ∧ (∀ i, i ≤ l → h (a i) = (((l:ℤ)-2*(i:ℤ):ℤ):F) • a i) ∧ (∀ r i, i ≤ l → X r (a i) = if r ≤ i then (((l-i+r).choose r : ℕ):F) • a (i-r) else 0) ∧ (∀ r i, i ≤ l → Y r (a i) = if i+r ≤ l then (((i+r).choose r : ℕ):F) • a (i+r) else 0)
def IsStringBasis {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (l : ℕ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (B : Module.Basis (Idx l) ℂ V) : Prop := ∀ i, B i = e y v i.val
structure IntegralOps {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) where
 xz : Module.End ℤ M
 yz : Module.End ℤ M
 hz : Module.End ℤ M
 Xz : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
 Yz : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
 x_agree : ∀ m, (xz m : V) = x m
 y_agree : ∀ m, (yz m : V) = y m
 h_agree : ∀ m, (hz m : V) = h m
 X_agree : ∀ r m, (Xz r m : V) = DP x r m
 Y_agree : ∀ r m, (Yz r m : V) = DP y r m
abbrev VK (K : Type*) [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def Jc (p : ℕ) {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (w : V) : Submodule (R p) ℂ := Submodule.span (R p) {c | c • w ∈ MR p M}
def pMR (p : ℕ) {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) (MR p M) := LinearMap.range ((p : R p) • (LinearMap.id : MR p M →ₗ[R p] MR p M))
abbrev QMR (p : ℕ) {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := (MR p M) ⧸ (pMR p M)
section Complex
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
def Strings (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
 (∀ m : ℕ, h ((y^m) v) = ((lam-2*(m:ℤ):ℤ):ℂ) • ((y^m) v)) ∧ (∀ m : ℕ, x ((y^(m+1)) v) = ((((m+1:ℕ):ℤ)*(lam-(m:ℤ)):ℤ):ℂ) • ((y^m) v))
def StringResult (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
 0 < lam.toNat+1 ∧ Fintype.card (Idx lam.toNat) = lam.toNat+1 ∧ Strings lam x y h v ∧ e y v 0 = v ∧ (∃ B : Module.Basis (Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B) ∧ (∀ m : ℕ, lam.toNat < m → (y^m) v = 0) ∧ Actions lam.toNat (e y v) x y h (DP x) (DP y)
structure LatticeEmbedding (p l : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) where
 basis : Module.Basis (Idx l) (R p) (MR p M)
 tensorEquiv : (R p ⊗[ℤ] M) ≃ₗ[R p] MR p M
 tensor_value : ∀ r m, (tensorEquiv (r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) : V) = (((r : R p) : ℚ) : ℂ) • (m : V)
 complex_span : Submodule.span ℂ (MR p M : Set V) = ⊤
def Preserves (p l : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
 Nonempty (IntegralOps M x y h) ∧ (∀ r m, m ∈ MR p M → DP x r m ∈ MR p M) ∧ (∀ r m, m ∈ MR p M → DP y r m ∈ MR p M) ∧ (∀ t, t ≤ l → IsUnit (t.factorial : R p)) ∧ (∀ j, j ≤ l → IsUnit (l.choose j : R p))
def MatrixControl (p l : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (B : Module.Basis (Idx l) ℂ V) : Prop :=
 (DP y l * DP x l = MU B ⟨l,Nat.lt_succ_self l⟩ ⟨l,Nat.lt_succ_self l⟩) ∧
 (∀ i : Idx l, DP x (l-i.val) * MU B ⟨l,Nat.lt_succ_self l⟩ ⟨l,Nat.lt_succ_self l⟩ = MU B i ⟨l,Nat.lt_succ_self l⟩) ∧
 (∀ j : Idx l, MU B ⟨l,Nat.lt_succ_self l⟩ ⟨l,Nat.lt_succ_self l⟩ * DP y (l-j.val) = ((l.choose j.val : ℕ):ℂ) • MU B ⟨l,Nat.lt_succ_self l⟩ j) ∧
 (∀ i j : Idx l, MU B i j = (((l.choose j.val : ℕ):ℂ)⁻¹) • (DP x (l-i.val) * DP y l * DP x l * DP y (l-j.val))) ∧
 (∀ i j : Idx l, ∀ m, m ∈ MR p M → MU B i j m ∈ MR p M)
def LocalResult (p l : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (B : Module.Basis (Idx l) ℂ V) : Prop := Nonempty (LatticeEmbedding p l M) ∧ Preserves p l M x y h ∧ MatrixControl p l M x y B
structure Decomposition (p l : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (v : V) (B : Module.Basis (Idx l) ℂ V) where
 exact_J : ∀ c : ℂ, c ∈ Jc p M v ↔ c • v ∈ MR p M
 exact_coord : ∀ i : Idx l, ∀ c : ℂ, c ∈ Jc p M (B i) ↔ c • B i ∈ MR p M
 common : ∀ i : Idx l, Jc p M (B i) = Jc p M v
 fg : (Jc p M v).FG
 nonzero : Jc p M v ≠ ⊥
 coordEquiv : (Idx l → Jc p M v) ≃ₗ[R p] MR p M
 coord_value : ∀ c, (coordEquiv c : V) = ∑ i, (c i : ℂ) • B i
abbrev T (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (v : V) := ℚ ⊗[R p] Jc p M v
def RationalEmbedding (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
 ∃ mu : T p M v →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ, (∀ q c, mu (q ⊗ₜ[R p] c) = (q : ℂ) * (c : ℂ)) ∧ Function.Injective mu ∧ Module.Finite ℚ (T p M v)
def CoordinateResult (p l : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (v : V) (B : Module.Basis (Idx l) ℂ V) : Prop :=
 0 < l+1 ∧ Nonempty (Decomposition p l M v B) ∧ RationalEmbedding p M v ∧ Module.finrank ℚ (T p M v) = 1 ∧ (∀ a c : ℂ, a ∈ Jc p M v → a ≠ 0 → c ∈ Jc p M v → ∃ q : ℚ, c = (q : ℂ) * a)
def PrincipalResult (p l : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (v : V) (B : Module.Basis (Idx l) ℂ V) : Prop :=
 (∃ b : ℂ, b ∈ Jc p M v ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧ Jc p M v = Submodule.span (R p) {b}) ∧ (∀ b : ℂ, b ∈ Jc p M v → b ≠ 0 → Jc p M v = Submodule.span (R p) {b} → ∃ f : Module.Basis (Idx l) (R p) (MR p M), ∀ i, (f i : V) = b • B i) ∧ 0 < l+1 ∧ Fintype.card (Idx l) = l+1
structure FirstChange (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) where
 [ak : Algebra (R p) K]
 rho_value : ∀ a b : ℤ, ∀ r : R p, (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ)/(b : ℚ) → ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b → algebraMap (R p) K r = (a : K)/(b : K)
 inc : M →ₗ[ℤ] MR p M
 inc_value : ∀ m, (inc m : V) = (m : V)
 A : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[R p] MR p M)
 A_value : ∀ c m, A (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = c ⊗ₜ[R p] inc m
structure ScalarData (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) extends FirstChange p K M where
 [af : Algebra (ZMod p) K]
 [mq : Module (ZMod p) (QMR p M)]
 residue : (R p ⧸ Ideal.span {(p : R p)}) ≃+* ZMod p
 residue_value : ∀ a b : ℤ, ∀ r : R p, (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ)/(b : ℚ) → ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b → residue (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ r) = (a : ZMod p) * (b : ZMod p)⁻¹
 C : (K ⊗[R p] MR p M) ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] QMR p M)
 C_value : ∀ c u, C (c ⊗ₜ[R p] u) = c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] (pMR p M).mkQ u
structure ReducedBasis (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (l : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (v : V) (B : Module.Basis (Idx l) ℂ V) where
 scalars : ScalarData p K M
 b : ℂ
 b_mem : b ∈ Jc p M v
 b_ne : b ≠ 0
 principal : Jc p M v = Submodule.span (R p) {b}
 f : Module.Basis (Idx l) (R p) (MR p M)
 f_value : ∀ i, (f i : V) = b • B i
 beta : Module.Basis (Idx l) K (VK K M)
 transported : letI := scalars.ak; ∀ i, scalars.A (beta i) = (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[R p] f i
 quotient_basis : letI := scalars.mq; ∃ gamma : Module.Basis (Idx l) (ZMod p) (QMR p M), ∀ i, gamma i = (pMR p M).mkQ (f i)
 dimension : Module.finrank K (VK K M) = l+1
 positive : 0 < l+1
 cardinality : Fintype.card (Idx l) = l+1
def ReducedAction (K : Type*) [Field K] (l : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (o : IntegralOps M x y h) (beta : Module.Basis (Idx l) K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
 Brackets (o.xz.baseChange K) (o.yz.baseChange K) (o.hz.baseChange K) ∧ Actions l (ext beta) (o.xz.baseChange K) (o.yz.baseChange K) (o.hz.baseChange K) (fun r => (o.Xz r).baseChange K) (fun r => (o.Yz r).baseChange K) ∧ (∀ r, r ≤ l → (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0 ∧ (o.Xz r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (o.xz.baseChange K)^r ∧ (o.Yz r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (o.yz.baseChange K)^r)
def ReducedControl (K : Type*) [Field K] (l : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (o : IntegralOps M x y h) (beta : Module.Basis (Idx l) K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
 (∀ i j : Idx l, MU beta i j = (((l.choose j.val : ℕ):K)⁻¹) • ((o.Xz (l-i.val)).baseChange K * (o.Yz l).baseChange K * (o.Xz l).baseChange K * (o.Yz (l-j.val)).baseChange K)) ∧ (∀ W : Submodule K (VK K M), Inv W (o.xz.baseChange K) → Inv W (o.yz.baseChange K) → ∀ i j, Inv W (MU beta i j))
def ReductionResult (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (l : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (B : Module.Basis (Idx l) ℂ V) : Prop :=
 ∃ rb : ReducedBasis p K l M v B, ∃ o : IntegralOps M x y h, ReducedAction K l M x y h o rb.beta ∧ ReducedControl K l M x y h o rb.beta
end Complex
end LR

premise_types.H004: Module.Finite ℂ V ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = lam.toNat+1 ∧ LR.Brackets x y h ∧ Nontrivial V ∧ ∀ W : Submodule ℂ V, LR.Inv W x → LR.Inv W y → LR.Inv W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
premise_types.H005: v ≠ 0 ∧ x v = 0 ∧ h v = (lam : ℂ) • v
premise_types.H006: (∃ f : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℤ M, ∃ c : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, ∀ i, (f i : V) = c i) ∧ (∀ r m, m ∈ M → LR.DP x r m ∈ M) ∧ (∀ r m, m ∈ M → LR.DP y r m ∈ M)

conclusion_type: Nontrivial (LR.VK K M) ∧ ∃ o : LR.IntegralOps M x y h, ∀ W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M), LR.Inv W (o.xz.baseChange K) → LR.Inv W (o.yz.baseChange K) → LR.Inv W (o.hz.baseChange K) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
representation: PENDING_AUDIT_B. Use action endomorphisms of the complex sl2 module; the three Chevalley brackets and common invariant subspaces encode its representation and irreducibility. lam remains an integer; l=lam.toNat and Idx l=Fin(l+1), with H003 justifying the identification. M is a Z-submodule of V (equivalently an additive subgroup). R is the subring of Q generated by fractions with p-prime denominators; T005 proves it is exactly Z_(p). MR is its span inside V; T006 constructs the tensor identification, not an assumed embedding. Jc is initially a span, and T009 proves its exact coordinate-set meaning. All tensor spaces are scalar-first: VK=K tensor_Z M is the canonical flip of the source M tensor_Z K. FirstChange/ScalarData record checked natural maps, not assumptions. IntegralOps records restrictions whose existence is proved, and baseChange gives the tensor-induced action. All result structures are witness records and their existence is a step obligation.

steps.statement: LR.Strings lam x y h v
steps.explanation: Induct on the nonnegative lowering exponent using the three commutators; the successor version of the raising formula includes the m=0 case.

steps.statement: (∀ i : LR.Idx lam.toNat, LR.e y v i.val ≠ 0) ∧ LinearIndependent ℂ (fun i : LR.Idx lam.toNat => LR.e y v i.val)
steps.explanation: Iterate raising to show nonvanishing. Isolate each coefficient using the product of h minus the other complex weights; all differences are nonzero in characteristic zero.

steps.statement: (∃ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B) ∧ (∀ m : ℕ, lam.toNat < m → (y^m) v = 0)
steps.explanation: Use dimension to upgrade independence to a basis. The next lowering vector has an absent eigenvalue, hence is zero in that basis; further powers vanish.

steps.statement: LR.StringResult lam x y h v
steps.explanation: Derive the basic x,y,h actions, then iterate and divide by factorials to obtain both integral binomial formulas, including the zero branches. Package N001.

steps.statement: ∀ q : ℚ, q ∈ LR.R p ↔ ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ)/(b : ℚ)
steps.explanation: Prove that fractions with p-prime denominators form a subring, so the closure definition of R has exactly the intended carrier. This is a checked representation bridge.

steps.statement: Nonempty (LR.LatticeEmbedding p lam.toNat M)
steps.explanation: The H006 basis is reindexed by Fin(l+1), equivalently the source reindexing by dimension. Base-change it to R. Complex independence proves injectivity of tensor multiplication and identifies its range with the R-span MR; obtain the displayed equivalence and complex spanning.

steps.statement: LR.Preserves p lam.toNat M x y h
steps.explanation: Restrict the divided powers to M and extend preservation to its R-span. Restrict h=[x,y]. Prime-to-p factorials and the binomial-factorial identity give all required units in R.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → LR.LocalResult p lam.toNat M x y h B
steps.explanation: Compute the three matrix-unit identities on the characteristic-zero basis. Invert the binomial unit in R and compose to show every coordinate matrix unit preserves MR. Package N002, including the proved tensor embedding and integral restrictions.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → Nonempty (LR.Decomposition p lam.toNat M v B)
steps.explanation: Prove the exact membership characterizations of the span-defined Jc objects. Matrix units identify all coordinate modules with J at e0=v. Projection of a finite basis gives finite generation; spanning gives nonzeroness. The coordinate sum defines the R-linear equivalence.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → LR.RationalEmbedding p M v
steps.explanation: Construct multiplication Q tensor_R J to C by balancing. Put finitely many rational tensor factors over one nonzero integer denominator to prove injectivity. Base-change a finite generating family to prove finite dimensionality.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → ∀ d : LR.Decomposition p lam.toNat M v B, ∃ Phi : (ℚ ⊗[LR.R p] LR.MR p M) ≃ₗ[ℚ] (LR.Idx lam.toNat → LR.T p M v), ∀ q c, Phi (q ⊗ₜ[LR.R p] d.coordEquiv c) = fun i => q ⊗ₜ[LR.R p] c i
steps.explanation: Rationalize the coordinate isomorphism. Define both maps by balanced tensor maps, with inverse the finite sum of the coordinate injections, and check their composites on elementary tensors.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → Module.finrank ℚ (LR.T p M v) = 1
steps.explanation: The rationalized localized lattice has dimension n from its R-basis. The checked coordinate isomorphism gives dimension n*r on the other side. Finite dimensionality and n>0 imply r=1.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → LR.CoordinateResult p lam.toNat M v B
steps.explanation: A nonzero a in J gives a nonzero rational tensor. Rank one makes it a rational basis; multiplication then expresses each c in J as a rational multiple of a. Package all of N003.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → ∃ k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ ∃ g : Fin k → ℂ, (∀ j, g j ∈ LR.Jc p M v ∧ g j ≠ 0) ∧ LR.Jc p M v = Submodule.span (LR.R p) (Set.range g)
steps.explanation: Choose finite generators of the nonzero module J and delete zero entries. Reindex the remaining nonempty finite list.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → ∀ (k : ℕ) (g : Fin k → ℂ), 0 < k → (∀ j, g j ∈ LR.Jc p M v ∧ g j ≠ 0) → ∃ a : ℂ, a ∈ LR.Jc p M v ∧ a ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ nu : Fin k → ℤ, ∃ u : Fin k → (LR.R p)ˣ, (∀ j, g j = ((((p : ℚ) ^ nu j) * ((u j : LR.R p) : ℚ) : ℚ) : ℂ) * a) ∧ ∃ j0 : Fin k, ∀ j, nu j0 ≤ nu j
steps.explanation: Use the rational-line assertion, factor each nonzero rational coefficient as p to an integer power times a unit of R, and choose the minimum exponent. The valuation/unit factorization may use the rational p-adic valuation library directly.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → LR.PrincipalResult p lam.toNat M v B
steps.explanation: The generator with minimum exponent gives b and J=Rb. The coordinate decomposition proves that b times every e_i is a basis. Repeat for any nonzero principal generator, as required by N004.

steps.statement: Nonempty (LR.FirstChange p K M)
steps.explanation: Construct rho by inverting p-prime denominators, and the natural scalar-first tensor associativity equivalence. Check its inverse and elementary tensor formula. The scalar-first convention is the canonical flip of the source convention.

steps.statement: Nonempty (LR.ScalarData p K M)
steps.explanation: Prove R/pR is ZMod p with its fraction formula. Give MR/pMR its canonical ZMod p module structure. Construct the second natural tensor equivalence by taking classes, with inverse independent of the lift because p acts as zero on K.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → Nonempty (LR.ReducedBasis p K lam.toNat M v B)
steps.explanation: Choose a principal generator and its localized basis. Base-change along rho and transport back along A to beta. Coordinate reduction gives the ZMod p quotient basis. Compute the dimension and positive cardinality.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → ∀ rb : LR.ReducedBasis p K lam.toNat M v B, ∀ o : LR.IntegralOps M x y h, LR.ReducedAction K lam.toNat M x y h o rb.beta
steps.explanation: The natural scalar maps intertwine restrictions and tensor extensions, checked on elementary tensors. Transfer the characteristic-zero formulas to b e_i and then beta. Tensor extension preserves brackets and the integer identities r! X_r=x^r and r! Y_r=y^r; the factorial images are nonzero.

steps.statement: ∀ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B → ∀ rb : LR.ReducedBasis p K lam.toNat M v B, ∀ o : LR.IntegralOps M x y h, LR.ReducedControl K lam.toNat M x y h o rb.beta
steps.explanation: Transfer the matrix-unit product identity to beta (or verify it there using the transferred formulas). A binomial unit stays nonzero. An x,y-stable K-subspace is stable under powers, scalar multiples, and all products appearing in that identity.

steps.statement: ∃ B : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) ℂ V, LR.IsStringBasis lam.toNat y v B ∧ LR.ReductionResult p K lam.toNat M x y h v B
steps.explanation: Choose the string basis and package the scalar identifications, quotient and reduced bases, tensor-induced operators, all reduced formulas, and matrix-unit invariance. This realizes the complete N005 output.

steps.statement: ∀ beta : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) K (LR.VK K M), Nontrivial (LR.VK K M) ∧ ∀ W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M), W ≠ ⊥ → ∃ w : LR.VK K M, w ∈ W ∧ w ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ j : LR.Idx lam.toNat, beta.repr w j ≠ 0
steps.explanation: Any such nonempty basis makes the space nonzero. In a nonzero subspace choose w≠0; injectivity of basis coordinates gives a nonzero coordinate.

steps.statement: ∀ beta : Module.Basis (LR.Idx lam.toNat) K (LR.VK K M), ∀ W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M), (∀ i j, LR.Inv W (LR.MU beta i j)) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
steps.explanation: In the nonzero branch, apply each coordinate matrix unit to w. Divide by its nonzero j-th coordinate to put every basis vector in W, so W is top.

steps.statement: Nontrivial (LR.VK K M) ∧ ∃ o : LR.IntegralOps M x y h, ∀ W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M), LR.Inv W (o.xz.baseChange K) → LR.Inv W (o.yz.baseChange K) → LR.Inv W (o.hz.baseChange K) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
steps.explanation: Use the N005 reduced basis for nonzeroness, and its matrix-unit invariance with the independent matrix-unit subspace lemma. Universally quantify over W. The generators span L(K), including characteristic 2; the singleton l=0 case requires no special argument. This is P.

P.explanation: All fields K of characteristic p and all complex action modules and arbitrary lattices are quantified as parameters with the six original hypotheses. The three bracket relations present sl2(C), and common x,y,h-invariant subspaces encode irreducibility; the highest weight vector and dimension are retained. A Z-submodule is exactly an additive subgroup, and its simultaneous integer/complex basis can be indexed by Fin(l+1) since dim V=l+1. Generator stability is equivalent to stability under the generated U_Z. With 0≤lam, l=lam.toNat equals lam, so the range and dimension are unchanged. Tensor flip identifies K tensor_Z M with M tensor_Z K in both directions, intertwining each induced operator. IntegralOps contains only restrictions agreeing on every lattice element; such restrictions are unique. The existential witness therefore states the actual induced action, not a selectable new action. Nontrivial is nonzeroness; bottom/top are zero/the whole space. Invariance under x,y,h is equivalent to invariance under their K-linear span L(K), also in characteristic 2. No algebraic closure or distinct reduced weights are imposed.
